nodes.label: Conservative Posed Bounds
nodes.rationale: Transforming the rest AABB corners by every palette matrix overestimates animated bounds at joint cost, which is safe for culling and avoids per-vertex work.

nodes.label: Parent-Before-Child Skeleton Invariant
nodes.rationale: Topologically sorting joints so every parent precedes its children makes model-space pose evaluation a deterministic single forward pass and requires remapping source joint indices.

nodes.label: Skin-to-Buffer
nodes.rationale: A compute pass writes posed vertices into the shared GeometryPool so culling, shading, shadows, and ray tracing consume animated geometry without learning about animation; the accepted cost is transient memory and bandwidth.

nodes.label: Luau Animation Command Boundary
nodes.rationale: Typed Luau callbacks emit neutral deferred animation-parameter commands, keeping engine pointers out of scripts and leaving schema validation in the animation runtime.

nodes.label: Pose-Renderer Boundary
nodes.rationale: Animation produces pose data and one system converts it to GPU palettes, allowing the renderer to remain independent of clips, graphs, ragdolls, and IK.

nodes.label: Shared Graph and Timeline Seam
nodes.rationale: Features contribute data-driven archetype catalogues to one graph surface and one timeline so materials, animation, VFX, and behavior trees do not fork editor infrastructure.

nodes.label: Budgeted Main-Thread Completion Drain
nodes.rationale: Workers produce data while the main thread installs it within a per-frame time budget, preventing bursts of completed background work from recreating frame hitches.

nodes.label: Priority and Deadline Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Priority remains dominant while earlier deadlines order equal-priority work and expired queued jobs are discarded, bounding speculative streaming thrash.

nodes.label: Recipe Dependency DAG
nodes.rationale: Canonical source and sorted dependency recipe hashes give deterministic artifacts and exact reverse-closure invalidation while excluding paths, timestamps, and cache locations.

nodes.label: Budgeted Residency Manager
nodes.rationale: Stable handles expose type-correct placeholders immediately, uploads span frames under a hard byte budget, and atomic swaps prevent consumers from observing partial revisions.

nodes.label: Cell Actor Ownership
nodes.rationale: Each streamed ECS actor is an independently stored schema document owned by one cell; unloading persists successfully before despawning so failed or cancelled work leaves live entities untouched.

nodes.label: Integer-Grid Floating Origin
nodes.rationale: Exact integer cells plus small local floats preserve centimeter differences at extreme distances without spreading soft-double arithmetic through shaders for planet-scale needs the shipped maps do not have.

nodes.label: Script Snapshot-In Commands-Out Ownership
nodes.rationale: Scripts read immutable snapshots and emit validated commands so structural changes cannot invalidate live archetype iteration and stale handles become typed rejections.

nodes.label: Generated Property Inspector
nodes.rationale: Generating Details rows from the component schema collapses hundreds of hand-maintained identifiers and makes serialization, scripting, editing, and undo share one field vocabulary.

nodes.label: Generic Field Command and Gesture Undo
nodes.norm_label: generic field command and gesture undo

nodes.label: Authored Material Identity and Derived Runtime State
nodes.norm_label: authored material identity and derived runtime state
nodes.rationale: Scenes persist stable material AssetIds while renderer pool and bindless indices remain derived session state, preventing unstable runtime identifiers from becoming authored data.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion and High Contrast Preferences
nodes.norm_label: reduced motion and high contrast preferences

nodes.label: Stateful Spring Motion
nodes.rationale: A physical spring carries velocity across retargeting, unlike a duration-normalized easing curve, so interrupted motion changes direction without visibly stopping first.

nodes.label: Embedded Curve Editor
nodes.rationale: The existing retained CurveEditor is embedded as the timeline's child so channel editing reuses one curve model and routes changes without shell forwarding.

nodes.label: Build the Engine Half Strategy
nodes.rationale: The renderer is only useful as an engine differentiator if games can animate characters, stream worlds, present UI, author content, and ship through public APIs.

nodes.label: CSM Measured Default
nodes.rationale: CSM remains the default because it measured faster than VSM on both shipped maps; VSM stays an explicit per-light quality and scaling choice.

nodes.label: Capture After Tonemapping
nodes.rationale: Display and editor evidence must be captured after tone mapping because raw HDR values do not produce meaningful PNG evidence.

nodes.label: Scene and Display Capture Split
nodes.rationale: UI-inclusive capture happens after the UI pass, while display capture happens before editor chrome so scene comparisons measure rendering rather than panels.

nodes.label: Measured Lockup Generation
nodes.rationale: Lockups are generated from outlined bundled fonts and measured artwork bounds to avoid platform font fallback, dead space, and clipping.

nodes.label: Hardware Ray Tracing as Primary Tier
nodes.norm_label: hardware ray tracing as primary tier
nodes.rationale: The existing bindless stack and target RTX hardware make ray query the smaller, higher-ceiling primary implementation; software SDF tracing remains a portability fallback.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Audio Mixer
nodes.rationale: A bus tree makes master and category gains composable, while mixer-level solo semantics avoid recomputing per-track state.

nodes.label: Nonfatal Audio Failure Policy
nodes.rationale: Missing content or unavailable audio hardware should yield diagnostics and silence rather than prevent a game from starting.

nodes.label: Application Mode and Viewport Command Scopes
nodes.norm_label: application mode and viewport command scopes

nodes.label: Safe Content Creation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Creation refuses overwrites and path traversal, while deletion is omitted because the drawer has no undo or recycle-bin recovery path.

nodes.label: Viking Boat Buoyancy Proxy
nodes.rationale: A stable box proxy and distributed surface queries avoid noisy triangle-mesh contact while keeping the high-detail hierarchy visual-only.

nodes.label: Clean-Room Reference Policy
nodes.rationale: Somnium studies third-party architecture but writes original Rust code; proprietary references may inform structure but cannot supply adapted code.

nodes.label: Study References, Do Not Copy
nodes.rationale: Contributors must cite studied references while keeping implementation original.

nodes.label: MORROWIND License Audit
nodes.rationale: Reference licensing must be measured at both repository root and the exact source-file header because Flax and Daemon changed tier under closer inspection.

nodes.label: Collapsed Accessibility Tree
nodes.rationale: Presentational scaffolding is collapsed and hidden subtrees omitted so assistive technology receives meaningful controls instead of mirroring every implementation wrapper.

nodes.label: Dual Selection Cues
nodes.rationale: Selection combines fill, rail, and type-weight changes so state is not communicated by color alone and hover does not reflow rows.

nodes.label: Budgeted Asynchronous Thumbnail Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Decode and downscale run off-thread while bounded generation and atlas writes run on the main thread, preventing large source images from freezing the editor.

nodes.label: Typed Drag Payload and Effect Seam
nodes.norm_label: typed drag payload and effect seam

nodes.label: Regenerable Census Gate
nodes.rationale: Generated measurements are authoritative over hand-typed historical baselines, and a build gate prevents architecture counts from silently becoming stale.

nodes.label: Deferred Script Commit Visibility
nodes.rationale: A script sees its own writes immediately but other scripts see them only after the phase commit, preventing authored execution order from becoming a hidden correctness dependency.

nodes.label: Literal Require Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: Restricting require to string literals lets reload, cooking, and cycle detection discover dependencies without executing scripts.

nodes.label: Canvas Space and Shaped Stream Seam
nodes.norm_label: canvas space and shaped stream seam

nodes.label: Present Adapt Refuse Defer Framework
nodes.rationale: Reference modules are classified before implementation so compatible gaps are adapted, incompatible architectural answers are refused, and already-solved systems are not rewritten.

nodes.label: Strict Reference Clean-Room Rule
nodes.rationale: Proprietary and copyleft references may inform architecture only; shipped implementation must avoid their identifiers, layouts, constants, comments, and code, and relevant file headers must be checked rather than assuming the root license governs.

nodes.label: Action-Based Input Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Keycodes are isolated in the device layer so bindings remain editable data, processors centralize analog behavior, interactions express gestures, and game code consumes device-independent action values.

nodes.label: Unkeyed String Extractor
nodes.rationale: Translation-file checks cannot detect UI literals that were never converted into keys, so source extraction must report both keys and unkeyed strings.

nodes.label: Single Description Principle
nodes.rationale: Composed shader identity, validation, and pass construction must share one source of truth because duplicated descriptions and version pins drift independently.

nodes.label: Transactional Shader Hot Reload
nodes.rationale: Changed modules are validated before installation; a failed reload preserves the prior source and pipeline and surfaces the diagnostic visibly instead of silently reverting.

nodes.label: CPU Path Tessellation
nodes.rationale: Somnium needs many short wires and curves rather than glyph-density vector fills, so CPU tessellation avoids introducing a second renderer and its scheduling and intermediate targets.

nodes.label: Shaped Instance Stream
nodes.rationale: A second ordered stream adds transforms, strokes, arbitrary textures, masks, and local-space gradients without reopening the frozen 100-byte quad instance contract.

nodes.label: Engine Owns the Render Moment
nodes.rationale: Games own any number of UI trees, while the engine exposes the safe frame moment and render resources needed to draw them without embedding one special canvas in EngineContext.

nodes.label: Region-Based Golden Images
nodes.rationale: Golden comparisons crop deterministic UI chrome regions so stochastic viewport content and transient state do not train developers to ignore unrelated failures.

nodes.label: Render-to-Texture World UI
nodes.rationale: World-space UI renders to an offscreen target consumed as a registered texture, preserving the frozen screen-space shader and visibility-buffer contracts at the cost of one resampling step.

nodes.label: Directional UI Navigation
nodes.rationale: Authored links override a geometry fallback whose scoring strongly favors alignment, combining maintainability in regular layouts with explicit control for exceptional topology.

nodes.label: Cosmic Text Shaper Decision
nodes.rationale: cosmic-text combines shaping with editing and cursor movement needed by IME, but adoption is gated on visual A/B evidence because subpixel advances can regress the editor's crisp block-origin snapping.

nodes.label: IME Composition Model
nodes.rationale: Preedit is provisional display state rather than committed text, and Enter must be swallowed while composition is active so confirming a word cannot submit a dialog.

nodes.label: Single Archetype-Driven Graph Surface
nodes.rationale: Material, animation, behavior, VFX, and scattering contribute catalogue data to one feature-neutral surface rather than creating parallel graph editors.
